payload.title: Board surprise E02: observed undiagnosed (HbA1c-only) below expected
payload.why_surprising: The expected value lies outside the 95% CI. The comparability label lists definition differences: CDC includes fasting glucose >= 126, is age-adjusted, and covers ages >= 18. Ranks 1, 2 and 6 show that glucose and HbA1c classify different people. Assessing whether the definitions are correct is left to the skeptic.

payload.title: Board surprise E03: observed prediabetes (HbA1c-only) below expected
payload.why_surprising: The expected value lies outside the 95% CI. The board labels comparability as low: the CDC denominator includes diagnosed adults, and CDC uses HbA1c or glucose. Assessing whether the definitions are correct is left to the skeptic.

payload.finding: check_definitions(E04) returns error: outcome 'hba1c < 6.5' labelled category 'normal' disagrees with ADA (normal HbA1c < 5.7). It folds prediabetes 5.7-6.4 into 'normal'. Domain also does not exclude diag=='yes', so self-reported diagnosed adults with HbA1c < 6.5 count as 'normal'. Board also lacks citation and comparability ('TODO'). Impact: as specified the item yields 0.8966 (calc_00062) vs 0.6399 under the ADA normal cut (calc_00063). Board is read-only; flagged for humans, no edit proposed.

check_definitions(E01) clean. Thresholds correct (HbA1c >= 6.5). Comparability label 'partial' correctly declares HbA1c-only vs CDC HbA1c-or-glucose, crude vs age-adjusted, >=20 vs >=18. Observed HbA1c-only 0.1427 [0.1298, 0.1556] (calc_00061); fasting-subsample version adding glucose >= 126 with wt_fast 0.1585 [0.1350, 0.1819] (calc_00060). Both CIs contain 0.132. No attack beyond the declared limitations.

check_definitions(E02) clean on thresholds. Two scope issues: (1) numerator uses diag == 'no' only; adults answering 'borderline' with HbA1c >= 6.5 are neither diagnosed nor counted as undiagnosed. Using diag != 'yes' gives 0.0241 [0.0191, 0.0292] (calc_00050) vs 0.0186 (calc_00004). Whether CDC counts 'borderline' as not diagnosed should be verified against the cited source by a human. (2) Statement says 'HbA1c >= 6.5%' but the expected 0.031 is CDC's HbA1c-or-fasting-glucose definition; comparability label 'partial' declares this.

check_definitions(E03) clean on thresholds (5.7 <= HbA1c < 6.5). But the statement 'Prediabetes by HbA1c' is paired with an expected value (CDC Table 5 definition 1, 36.5%) that per the comparability label uses HbA1c 5.7-6.4 OR fasting glucose 100-125, is age-adjusted, covers ages >= 18, and includes diagnosed adults in the denominator. The expected value is not an HbA1c-only quantity, so the board item compares unlike definitions. Label 'low' is honest; quantified under the L0012 attack.

Reproduced: 0.6656 [0.531, 0.800], n=104, events=61, wt_fast correct (calc_00039); power passes (calc_00036). Threshold: at glucose >= 140 the share is 0.475 [0.217, 0.733] but only 16 events (calc_00037, calc_00040), so it is not confirmable there. At HbA1c < 6.0 the share is 0.424, 35 events (calc_00038). Measurement error: 0.579 of the cell has glucose 126-139 (calc_00041), i.e. near the cut-point on a single fasting draw. Fasting compliance and single-sample variability are not checkable here. HbA1c in this cross-tab is weighted with wt_fast, which is acceptable for the fasting subsample. Confounding by age/BMI not assessable at this cell size. The discordance is real but driven mostly by near-threshold glucose; it survives only as a measurement-agreement finding, not as a population quantity.

Both cells pass power: glucose-diabetes cell 406/111 (calc_00025); HbA1c-diabetes cell n=372, events=77 (calc_00058, the separate check the scout omitted). Weights (wt_fast) correct for cross-tabs involving glucose. Caveats: (a) these cells include diag=='yes' adults, whose medication can move glucose and HbA1c differently; (b) single measurement of each marker; (c) the 'larger in the glucose-to-HbA1c direction' claim compares two conditional shares with different denominators, which is no test of asymmetry, so it should be dropped. Core descriptive point (the markers classify different people) holds.

Power passes 159/40 (calc_00051). Threshold sensitivity is large: HbA1c >= 6.3 gives 0.246 with 50 events (calc_00053), and HbA1c >= 6.7 gives 0.087 with 26 events (calc_00052, < 30). Most events sit within 0.2 points of the 6.5 cut, so a single HbA1c measurement error matters. The definitional point is valid and feeds the E02 attack (L0015): including borderline moves undiagnosed from 0.0186 (calc_00004) to 0.0241 (calc_00050). As a standalone discovery it is weak; as a definition flag it holds.

Crude PR reproduced 1.734 [1.097, 2.741] (calc_00045). Threshold: robust at HbA1c >= 6.3 PR 1.744 [1.024, 2.970] (calc_00047) and >= 6.7 PR 2.031 [1.107, 3.727] (calc_00048, exposed events 23 < 30). Confounding: within pir < 2 PR 1.071 [0.417, 2.750] (calc_00044, exposed events 19), so income may account for the contrast; age < 45 PR 1.716 [0.769, 3.831] (calc_00042, 10 events); age >= 45 PR 2.467 [1.426, 4.268] (calc_00043, 21 events); BMI >= 30 PR 1.651 [0.839, 3.249] (calc_00049, 19 events). Every stratum has < 30 exposed events, so it cannot be confirmed within strata. Outcome definition: with glucose >= 126 (wt_fast) PR 0.847 [0.417, 1.721] (calc_00046, 11 events), so the direction does not replicate on the other marker. Routine-place null comparison (calc_00017, calc_00026) has 29 exposed events, below the gate, and is uninformative. Independent-SE log-PR approximation is a further declared limitation.

Cell 1 (diag yes, HbA1c < 5.7): power passes 804/47 (calc_00024). Expected mechanism: glucose-lowering medication lowers HbA1c, so HbA1c < 5.7 in diagnosed adults is not discordant by definition. Restricted to those with no insulin or pills declared currently: 0.263 [0.102, 0.425] but only 22 events (calc_00054), below the gate. Threshold: HbA1c < 5.5 gives 0.035 with 23 events (calc_00055), so the cell is concentrated near 5.7. Cell 2 (no insulin or pills declared currently, 0.168, calc_00012) is an expected feature of diagnosed populations (diet/lifestyle management, and the item covers current insulin/pills only), so it is no anomaly. Not a confirmatory candidate.

n=67, events=24 < MIN_CELL_N=30 (calc_00056; calc_00021). Not eligible for confirmatory use. Note: check_power returned passes=true with only a warning for events < 30. The gate apparently checks n only, while the lab rule requires >= 30 for both n and events. Flagged for humans as a tool-gate inconsistency.

n=1251, events=21 < MIN_CELL_N=30 (calc_00057; calc_00022). A three-way discordant cell defined by a single fasting glucose is the cell most exposed to measurement error and non-fasting misclassification. Not eligible for confirmatory use. Same check_power gate inconsistency (passes=true with events < 30).

The gap is a definition artifact. With the CDC-style outcome (diag 'no' and (HbA1c >= 6.5 or fasting glucose >= 126)) in the fasting subsample with wt_fast: 0.0349 [0.0259, 0.0439] (calc_00059), and the CI contains the expected 0.031. Including 'borderline' with HbA1c-only gives 0.0241 (calc_00050). Remaining differences (crude vs age-adjusted, >=20 vs >=18, 2017-2018 vs 2017-Mar 2020) are declared in the comparability label. The pipeline check passes once definitions match; this is not a discrepancy to investigate.

checks: definitions/comparability (domain, outcome, age range, age adjustment, glucose)
payload.finding: Reproduced 0.2560 [0.2330, 0.2791] (calc_00027). (1) Domain: switching to all adults (incl. diagnosed) barely moves it, 0.2567 (calc_00029), so the denominator does not explain the gap. (2) Outcome/glucose: CDC definition 1 uses HbA1c OR fasting glucose. With wt_fast, HbA1c 5.7-6.4 or glucose 100-125 (excluding diabetes range) gives 0.5979 [0.5532, 0.6427] (calc_00028), and glucose 100-125 alone gives 0.5562 (calc_00031). The expected 0.365 lies between the HbA1c-only and either-marker estimates, so neither definition reproduces it. The either-marker estimate overshoots and needs a pipeline check (glucose units/fasting filter/wt_fast domain) before any interpretation. (3) Age: strong gradient, age >= 45 vs < 45 PR 2.619 [2.193, 3.128] (calc_00035), so crude vs age-adjusted matters; age adjustment was not computed here. Ages 18-19 are excluded by the base domain and cannot be tested. (4) Threshold sensitivity is extreme: lower cut 5.6 gives 0.348 [0.321, 0.375] (calc_00032), and 5.8 gives 0.184 (calc_00033). A 0.1-point shift in the HbA1c cut or assay calibration moves the estimate by about as much as the gap, so a single-HbA1c, cut-point-driven gap cannot be confirmed. (5) Weights: HbA1c-only in the fasting subsample uses wt_mec automatically (calc_00030); for a fasting-subsample comparison wt_fast should be used, so calc_00030 is not a valid comparator. Conclusion: the board-vs-data gap is dominated by definition mismatch (statement says HbA1c-only, source is HbA1c-or-glucose) and cut-point sensitivity. It is not ready for confirmatory testing. A valid confirmatory question must first fix one definition and match the CDC definition, age range and age standardization.
